question: What is the primary focus of Human-Computer Interaction in nursing informatics?

options.A: How software engineers write computer code
options.B: How nurses communicate with digital technology
options.C: How computers diagnose complex medical diseases
options.D: How hospital networks share data globally

explanation: HCI studies the communication and interaction points between human users and technological systems. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h1)

question: Good HCI design in a hospital ward primarily helps nurses achieve what outcome?

options.B: Spend more quality time on direct patient care
options.C: Reduce the total number of hospital staff needed
options.D: Completely eliminate the need for paper records

explanation: Effective system design reduces administrative friction, freeing up time for clinical duties. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h1)

question: What does usability measure in healthcare software systems?

options.B: How fast the computer processor runs
options.C: The financial cost of buying the software
options.D: Network speed and server storage capacity

explanation: Usability evaluates how well and comfortably a user can accomplish tasks using a tool. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why should clinical software use familiar medical terminology instead of computer jargon?

options.A: It matches the mental model of the healthcare provider
options.B: It makes the software file size much smaller
options.C: It eliminates the need for internet connectivity
options.D: It prevents the computer system from crashing

explanation: Systems are easier to learn and use when they reflect the actual language and workflow of the clinician. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which interface type is most suitable for bedside vital sign entry during ward rounds?
explanation: Mobile devices allow nurses to input patient data directly at the bedside while moving through the ward. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h3)

question: A nurse needs to document wound care findings immediately while maintaining sterile gloves during a procedure. Which interface would be most useful?
explanation: Voice recognition allows hands-free data entry when physical contact with a screen or keyboard is restricted. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is cognitive load in the context of clinical workflows?

options.A: The speed at which a computer processes data files
options.B: The total number of patients admitted to a ward
options.C: The amount of mental effort used in working memory
options.D: The physical weight of carrying a computer around

explanation: Cognitive load measures how hard the human brain is working to process information at a given time. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h4)

question: Too many flashing alerts on a poorly designed computer screen will most likely cause what reaction?

options.A: Cognitive overload and potential clinical errors
options.B: Better retention of complex medical histories
options.D: Faster completion of patient documentation tasks

explanation: Excessive visual stimuli overwhelm working memory, increasing the risk of missed details and mistakes. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common usability barrier in clinical software?
explanation: Clear error messages support usability, whereas confusing menus, poor contrast, and vague alerts represent barriers. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why are forced confirmation fields useful when a nurse enters high-risk medication doses?

options.A: They test the typing speed of the attending nurse
options.B: They force the hospital to buy more pharmaceutical supplies
options.C: They slow down the computer network to save server space
options.D: They prevent accidental dosing errors through a double-check step

explanation: Confirmation prompts interrupt impulsive actions, giving clinicians a chance to catch potential mistakes. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why must nurses be actively involved in the design of healthcare software?

options.A: They are trained software engineering experts
options.B: They are the primary end-users of the systems
options.C: They purchase the hospital network servers
options.D: They maintain the physical computer hardware

explanation: Because nurses use these tools daily, their practical insights ensure the software fits actual clinical needs. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h6)

question: What happens when healthcare software is built without consulting clinical nurses?

options.A: It eliminates all documentation errors instantly
options.B: It lowers the financial cost of hospital operations
options.C: It becomes much faster and easier to operate
options.D: It often fails to match real-world ward workflows

explanation: Without clinical input, developers create systems that do not align with the practical realities of patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h6)
